summary: Runs a GLSL compute shader over one POP attribute class at a time: points, vertices, or primitives. It can create and modify attributes, drive dispatch sizing from inputs or attributes, expose shader uniforms/samplers/temp buffers/constants, and use collision acceleration structures, but it cannot change the number of input elements.

key_concepts: Copy Previous Pass Output to Input
common_gotchas: GLSL POP operates on one attribute class and cannot change point, vertex, or primitive counts; use GLSL Advanced POP when topology, index buffers, or output counts must change.
In Manual Number of Elements and automatic modes, guard writes with TDIndex() and TDNumElements() because TouchDesigner rounds actual dispatches up to the workgroup size.
In Manual mode, where workgroup size and dispatch size are specified in three dimensions, TDIndex() and TDNumElements() are undefined and will cause compile errors.
For P[id] writes, P must exist or be created and must be included in Output Attributes so the output buffer is allocated.

Output attributes are uninitialized unless Initialize Output Attributes is enabled or the shader writes every output value; reading uninitialized attributes can cause unpredictable behavior and crashes.
Use Read-Write output access when the shader needs to read output attributes or perform atomic operations; otherwise prefer writeonly SSBO intent.
Use TDInPoint_AttribName(), TDInPrim_AttribName(), or TDInVert_AttribName() when reading from a class other than the selected Attribute Class.
When Delete Input Attributes is enabled, downstream POPs only receive attributes that were explicitly output, so preserve any attributes the branch still needs.
Collision POP acceleration structures require matching shader ray-query code and a build strategy suited to dynamic or static geometry.
Inspect Info CHOP/operator errors for shader warnings and compile failures before treating empty geometry as a POP logic problem.
